participants.note: ACK modulo weird situation when resending resolved transactions; earlier concerns resolved
Concept ACK, but raised concerns about memory retention, dead retry code, and Remove slot handling

claims.harm: a transaction is marked as received when it has not actually been received
claims.quote: Why replace Remove() with MarkReceived() here? The transaction has not been actually received.
claims.after_reply_note: addressed by author rename to MarkResolved and confirmed by ACK

claims.harm: the send_limit counter is incremented for a stale transaction even if it still has unused allowance
claims.quote: This increments the send_limit counter for a transaction that came from GetStale() and is acceptable in the mempool. However such a transaction might still have unused "allowance".
claims.after_reply_note: author added check before granting retry connection, confirmed by ACK

claims.harm: NumToOpenAdd call is redundant when stale retry logic already runs frequently enough to pick up failed sends
claims.quote: we do not need the NumToOpenAdd(1) call here at all.
claims.after_reply_note: author explained why NumToOpenAdd is necessary and reviewer approved

claims.harm: a resolved transaction cannot be resent or scheduled again even though it is no longer queued or actively broadcast
claims.quote: This is a weird situation for the user: Trying to resend a transaction is refused with "Ignoring unnecessary request to schedule an already scheduled transaction"

claims.harm: retry logic becomes effectively dead code because reaching 1000 resend attempts takes impractically long
claims.quote: Now the retry is basically dead code, since it will take a long time until 1000 resend attempts are reached - I think it might as well be removed.

claims.harm: transactions are kept in memory indefinitely until node restart or maximum limit, increasing resource usage
claims.quote: This would lead to a potential unexpected increase in resource usage - before, we'd only keep transactions while they were in flight, and the shared pointer would be released
claims.after_reply_note: author noted the tradeoff avoiding extra disconnect tracking and asked for reviewer preference

claims.harm: a peer disconnecting without answering pong could cause Remove() to steal connection retry slots from unrelated transactions
claims.quote: now a peer that completed the handshake (`fDisconnect=true`) but doesn't answer the pong would not get a `peer_ack`, but also wouldn't get a try back, so if we then call `Remove()` it could steal slots from other, unrelated transactions.
